correctness.rationale: The classical complete 48-line list consists of three coordinate-pairing families of 16 lines; each pair of line equations yields an exact 4×4 cyclotomic determinant condition. Checking all 1128 unordered pairs gives 144 within-family and 192 cross-family edges; 48 vertices have degree 14 and the graph is connected. Independently reconstructed modular-congruence adjacency and verified the exact eigenvalue multiplicities 14^1,2^28,(-2)^12,(-6)^6,(-10)^1 (annihilating polynomial/trace method); matrix-tree theorem gives 2^115 3^28 5^6. On the 47×47 reduced Laplacian exact local p-adic Smith elimination gives p=2 valuations (0:18,2:12,3:5,6:8,7:4), p=3 (0:20,1:26,2:1), p=5 (0:41,1:6). Sorted factorwise valuations produce exactly the stated 47 invariants with determinant/product match and exponent 5760. All calculations are exact finite arithmetic, not floating point or inference from eigenvalues alone. The completeness of the 48 geometric lines is the explicitly cited classical theorem.

Their integral graph Jacobian is a natural finite invariant which is not recovered from the graph spectrum or Néron–Severi discriminant; a full Smith classification supplies data relevant to chip-firing and arithmetic graph comparisons. This is motivated finite structural mathematics rather than an arbitrary graph slice.

final_claim: The 48 geometric lines on the complex Fermat quartic x₀⁴+x₁⁴+x₂⁴+x₃⁴=0 form a connected 14-regular intersection graph with reduced Laplacian Smith factors 1^18,4^2,12^10,24^5,192^6,960^2,1920^3,5760. Its critical group has order 2^115·3^28·5^6 and exponent 5760.
limitations: Only complex Fermat quartic 48 embedded projective lines, with intersection as geometric adjacency; not arbitrary quartic K3s.
Graph critical group is not Néron–Severi torsion, its discriminant group, or the Jacobian of a curve.
